pageCache.pageTitle: Fielding Primary School & Nursery - Values Baccalaureate
pageCache.text:
Values Baccalaureate
Pupils in years 4, 5 and 6 work towards the Fielding Values Baccalaureate. To achieve this, pupils must demonstrate how they have used our four core values across the school, home and local & wider community. This empowers pupils to apply their learning about values in a range of ways and for these Values to further become part of their character.
There are four levels of the Baccalaureate:
These levels give pupils opportunities to apply and sustain the values ethos and learning over a long period of time, in a range of situations. Pupils are required to complete task cards and provide evidence for the stages. They can choose how they collect and show this evidence. Success within each level is celebrated as part of our Monday school assemblies. Pupils receive a patch to wear on their school jumper, recognising their achievement.
Evidence should be submitted to your class teacher. In portfolio form (A folder or collection of work).

About Us
We welcome children aged 3–11 from the Northfields community in Ealing.
Fielding is a vibrant, inclusive school where children thrive. With excellent teaching and a rich curriculum, we help every child achieve their best—academically, socially, and emotionally.
Children join us in Nursery or Reception, or transfer from other schools and countries. Everyone is welcome.
We’re proud of our spacious site, modern facilities, and happy, purposeful atmosphere. Our large field supports a wide range of sports and outdoor play. Children also enjoy gardening in our Kitchen Garden and caring for our hens.
Our values—respect, resilience, empathy and reflection —guide everything we do.
All children wear our school uniform and are encouraged to walk, cycle, or scoot to school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fielding Primary School & Nursery - Values-based education
pageCache.text:
Values-based education
At Fielding, we believe that values-based living is the foundation of a thriving and supportive community. Our approach centres around embedding key values—respect, resilience, reflection, and empathy—into every aspect of school life. By integrating these values into our teaching, interactions, and daily routines, we create an environment where children not only succeed academically but also develop essential life skills. Through activities like the Mind UP curriculum and a focus on emotional well-being, we work together with families to ensure that children grow into compassionate, thoughtful, and resilient individuals who contribute positively to society.
At Fielding, we promote an educational philosophy that values self, others, and the environment. Our approach is rooted in ethical principles that guide behaviour and decision-making.
Adults model these values and create space for reflection, helping pupils become confident learners and responsible citizens. Through this, children develop:
Our values-based approach supports the promotion of fundamental British values, including:
Assemblies and school events enrich pupils’ spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development, helping them build a clear sense of right and wrong.
We have four core school values that guide children's choices, behaviour and learning. These values are the basis of all our values teaching and will help children understand connected values.
Our core values are:
These values have been chosen by carefully observing and discussing which of our previous values have worked well and which ones would develop children the most morally and educationally.
Children in the early years start by focusing on just the core values. As pupils move through years 1 to 6 we begin to widen their understanding of each core value by connecting with similar values. The focus with every value is what the value looks like to us and how it looks in action. Teaching of values is cyclical. We return to each core value frequently to deepen understanding.
The value of sustainability also underpins our wider curriculum, this is weaved through our learning challenges in all age-groups.
At Fielding, we use the MindUP curriculum to teach social and emotional learning. Based on neuroscience, positive psychology, and mindfulness, MindUP helps pupils:
Through regular lessons and daily mindfulness practices, pupils learn to reflect, stay calm, and concentrate—skills that support both wellbeing and academic success.
Find out more about MindUP
"Values and MindUP helps me to feel safer on the inside", Year 6 pupil
At Fielding, there are no outsiders. We celebrate difference and teach children that diversity is something to be valued.
We use the No Outsiders programme to help children understand and respect all members of our community. Through age-appropriate picture books, pupils explore themes such as:
These lessons align with our school values—respect, resilience, reflection, and empathy—and are closely linked to our RSHE curriculum and Monday assemblies.
Frequently Asked Questions
What if my child asks, “How do two men have a baby?” Families are formed in many ways—through birth, fostering, or adoption. What matters is love and care.
Are children too young to learn about gay and lesbian relationships? We teach children to respect all people, including those in same-sex families. Some of our pupils live in these families and deserve to see themselves represented.
Are you teaching “gay lessons”? No. We are teaching about equality, as required by British law.
Can I withdraw my child from these lessons? No. Relationships education is statutory. If you have concerns, please speak with your child’s teacher.
What if my religion disagrees with this? We respect all beliefs. Our role is to teach children that diversity exists in society, even if individual beliefs differ.

Inclusion, SEN&D and Local Offer
Every Child Belongs. Every Child Participates. Every Child Achieves. Every Child Thrives.
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. It is not a separate programme or something that happens only for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). It is about creating a school where every child feels valued, supported and able to succeed.
Our Inclusion Strategy sets out how we remove barriers to learning, participation and wellbeing for all pupils, including those with SEND, those who are disadvantaged and those who may need additional support at different points in their school journey.
We recognise that children thrive when they:
Our approach is built around six key pillars:
The strategy also reflects national developments in SEND and inclusion. Rather than focusing solely on interventions or labels, we focus on understanding and removing the barriers that may prevent a child from fully participating in school life.
We are committed to working in partnership with children, families and professionals to ensure every child receives the support they need to flourish.
You can read our full Inclusion Strategy below.
We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where barriers to learning, participation and wellbeing are identified early and addressed through high-quality teaching, strong relationships and the right support at the right time. [
Our approach to SEND sits within our wider Inclusion Strategy and is built around a graduated response, ensuring that support follows need and helps pupils develop increasing independence.
Fielding follows a graduated approach to support.
High-quality adaptive teaching and ordinarily available provision for all pupils.
Additional support and short-term interventions for pupils who need more help than can be provided through classroom adaptations alone.
We are currently refining our structured specialist-informed support for pupils whose needs are not being fully met through Universal and Targeted provision. This may include support for communication and interaction, social and emotional needs, cognition and learning, or sensory and physical needs.
Support for pupils with the most complex needs, including Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) and our Additional Resource Provision (ARP).
In line with the SEND Code of Practice, support may be provided across four broad areas:
Many pupils experience needs across more than one area, and support is always tailored to the individual child.
We know that children make the best progress when school, home and external professionals work together. We actively seek the views of children and families and believe that successful support is developed with families, not for families.

Music Plan
What is the Music Development Plan? Our Music Development Plan outlines how we deliver high-quality music education across the school, from Nursery to Year 6, including our Additional Resource Provision (ARP). It sets out our curriculum approach, enrichment opportunities, and inclusive practices to ensure every child can enjoy and succeed in music. The plan also highlights how we assess progress, support pupils with SEND, and provide access to instrumental tuition, live performances, and music clubs. It helps us continuously improve our provision and celebrate the musical achievements of all pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fielding Primary School & Nursery - Overnight & residential trips
pageCache.text:
Overnight & residential trips
At Fielding Primary School, we believe that education extends far beyond the classroom. Our residential trips programme is a carefully planned and progressive part of our curriculum that supports children's personal development, helping them grow into confident, resilient and independent young people who feel a strong sense of belonging within our school community.
Beginning in Year 3 and culminating in a residential experience in France in Year 6, every child takes part in a journey that develops courage, character and confidence through shared experiences and challenge.
Our residential programme has been designed to ensure that children experience increasing levels of independence as they move through the school.
Year 3: Camp Out Under the Stars Children spend a night camping on the school field, enjoying outdoor challenges, bushcraft and campfire activities. For many, this is their first experience of sleeping away from home. Being on the familiar school site provides reassurance while helping children take those important first steps towards independence.
Year 4: Hooke Court, Dorset, new for 2027! Children travel further afield for a two-night camping experience linked to their geography learning. Through coastal studies, river investigations and learning about farming and food production, they begin to experience the excitement and responsibility of a residential stay away from home.
Year 5: Isle of Wight Our three-night residential at PGL Little Canada develops teamwork, cooperation and resilience. Children challenge themselves through adventurous outdoor activities whilst learning to live and work alongside their peers in a completely new environment.
Year 6: Burgundy, France The programme culminates in a five-night visit to France. Here, children put into practice the French they have been learning since Reception, experience another culture first-hand and apply geographical fieldwork skills in a real-world setting. It is a truly memorable way to celebrate the end of their primary school journey.
Through residential experiences, children learn to:
These experiences often enable children to discover strengths they did not know they possessed. Whether it is sleeping away from home for the first time, speaking French in a local market, overcoming a fear of heights or supporting a friend through a challenge, these moments help shape children's character and prepare them for future success.
We want every child to feel that they are an important part of the Fielding community. Residential trips create shared experiences that strengthen friendships, build year group identity and create memories that children talk about for years to come.
Living, learning and taking on challenges together helps children develop a deep sense of connection with their peers and with the school itself. They return with increased confidence, stronger relationships and a greater understanding of what it means to be part of a supportive community.
Importantly, our expectation is that every child can participate. We work hard to remove barriers to attendance, offering financial support and flexible payment arrangements where needed. We never want cost to prevent a child from accessing these life-enhancing experiences.
Our residential programme is not simply a collection of visits. It is a four-year journey of personal growth, carefully crafted to build confidence, independence and belonging step by step.
By the time children leave Fielding, they do so with not only wonderful memories, but also the confidence, resilience and life skills that will help them thrive in secondary school and beyond.
For many pupils, these experiences become some of the most treasured memories of their time at Fielding and among the moments that define what it means to be part of our school family. Find out more about each trip here:
